note: Breaking events for Neta. Satire only: every person, party and company is invented. Effects use the same keys as the rest of the game (pop, media, loy, white, black, corr, heat, scandal, karma, stress, rival, b:{far,you,tra,urb,wom,wor}).

events.title: Seven exit polls, seven answers
events.text: Every channel has an exit poll. Each one gives a different party a landslide. One poll has your party at 140% of the seats.

ch.r: The laddoos arrived before the results did.
Your statement was itself sponsored, by your own party.
Silence. The anchors found it suspicious.

events.title: A deepfake of you is dancing
events.text: A video of you dancing at a wedding you never attended has 4 million views. The dancing is better than yours.

ch.r: The cyber cell asked you to forward the video to them. Forty times.
You are now booked for three weddings.

ch.l: Make a deepfake of the rival
ch.r: His video is worse. Yours is still trending.

events.title: Onions cost more than petrol
events.text: Onion prices have tripled. A vendor in your constituency is selling them on EMI.

ch.r: The queue was longer than the onion supply.
The hoarders sent you a sack of onions. As a warning.
The clip was set to music by evening.

events.title: Heatwave on polling day
events.text: It is 47 degrees. Voters want water, shade and a reason to step out.

ch.r: Your booths had the coldest water and the warmest welcome.
The caps were confiscated. The umbrellas were not.
A photo of you in a cooled car went viral for the wrong reasons.

events.title: The team wins the World Cup
events.text: The national team has won. Every leader in the country is rushing to be in the trophy photo.

ch.r: You are in the photo, partly. Your left ear is very popular.

ch.l: Announce a stadium in your name
ch.r: The players were asked about it. They smiled politely.
Your tweet had a typo in the captain's name.

events.title: Chatbots take the call-centre jobs
events.text: A call-centre park in the city has replaced half its staff with an AI that speaks eleven languages and never asks for a raise.

ch.r: The mission's website was built by the same AI.
You read the speech off a chatbot. Someone noticed.

ch.l: Invest quietly in the AI firm
ch.r: Your stake tripled. So did the questions.

events.title: The new bridge falls before its opening
events.text: A bridge that was due to be inaugurated next week has collapsed into the river. The ribbon is still on order.

ch.r: The engineer was suspended. The contractor got the rebuild contract.

ch.s: Clean, but your party funds that contractor.
ch.r: The audit found the cement was mostly sand. And confidence.
The weather office released a statement: 'It was calm.'

events.title: The pothole that has its own fan page
events.text: A pothole on the main road is now big enough for ducks. Someone has opened an Instagram account for it. It has more followers than you.

ch.r: The ducks have filed a complaint.
You cut a ribbon over the water. The clip did numbers.
The pothole account is now endorsing your rival.

events.title: UPI goes down on salary day
events.text: The payments network is down for three hours on the 1st. Chai stalls are accepting IOUs. One accepts your autograph.

ch.r: The 'cyberattack' was a software update. Nobody corrected you.

ch.l: Pay the chai stall in cash, on camera
ch.r: You paid ₹20 in coins. The clip did better than your manifesto.
A probe was announced. It will report after the next outage.

events.title: Your nephew bids at the cricket auction
events.text: A franchise owned by 'a family friend' just paid ₹27 crore for a bowler. The paddle was held by your nephew.

ch.r: The nephew posted a selfie from the owner's box. With you in it.

ch.l: Throw the first ball at their match
ch.r: Your ball went wide. The crowd cheered anyway. The franchise's share price went up.
You watched on TV. Your nephew watched from the dugout.

events.title: 48°C and the minister's AC is on TV
events.text: A reporter filmed a minister's office with four ACs on and the door open. Outside, a power cut has lasted nine hours.

ch.l: Order cooling centres in every ward
ch.r: Water coolers arrived in 2 days. The photo of you drinking from one arrived in 2 minutes.
The clip trended with the hashtag #CharacterBuilding.

ch.l: Switch off your own AC, live
ch.r: You sat in the heat for an hour on camera. Then the AC came back on. The camera was off by then.

events.title: A minister's reel goes more viral than the budget
events.text: Your colleague lip-synced a film song in the Assembly corridor. It has 40 million views. The budget speech has 4,000.

ch.r: Your reel has 2 million views and one angry editorial.
The youth called you 'uncle'. Not affectionately.

ch.l: Explain the budget in a reel
ch.r: Your 60-second budget explainer was the most watched budget content ever. That's not saying much.

events.title: The stadium gets renamed mid-match
events.text: At the innings break, the scoreboard announced the stadium now has a new name. The commentators are confused. So is the stadium.

ch.l: Suggest your own name for it
ch.r: The scoreboard now reads your name. The players asked for a new pitch instead.

ch.l: Ask for the old name back
ch.r: A committee was formed. It meets at the stadium. Under the new name.

ch.l: Stay quiet and eat the samosa
ch.r: The samosa was excellent. The controversy was not your problem.

events.title: AI teachers in government schools
events.text: The state has announced an AI tutor in every classroom. Most classrooms do not have electricity.

ch.r: Your schools got fans and lights. The AI tutor is still 'coming soon'.
The tutor answered every question with 'please check your connection'.

ch.l: Ask the AI to write your speech
ch.r: The speech was flawless. It thanked 'the honourable user'.

events.title: A flyover opens, then closes for repairs
events.text: A flyover was inaugurated on Monday and shut on Tuesday 'for routine maintenance'. It has been routine for six weeks.

ch.l: Demand an audit of the contractor
ch.r: The contractor is now building a new flyover. In another district.
You cut a ribbon on the repair work. The ribbon was the only finished thing.
Truckers went on strike. The flyover remained empty, technically fixing the problem.

events.title: A billionaire's wedding shuts the city
events.text: A tycoon's son's wedding has closed four roads, the airport and one lake. Guests include three ex-PMs and a pop star from abroad.

ch.r: You danced near the pop star. The photo crop removed you.
Commuters loved it. The tycoon's channel stopped inviting you.

ch.l: Send a gift and stay home
ch.r: Your silver bowl was placed next to 900 other silver bowls.

events.title: The cheetahs leave the park
events.text: Two cheetahs walked out of the national park and into a village. They have been seen at a dhaba.

ch.l: Rush to the village with cameras
ch.r: The cheetahs left before you arrived. You were photographed with a very confused goat.

ch.l: Fund a fence and ranger jobs
ch.r: Thirty villagers got ranger jobs. The cheetahs got a fence. Everybody got a plan.
#CheetahYatra trended. The cheetahs did not comment.

events.title: Your party's group chat leaks
events.text: Screenshots of your party's WhatsApp group are everywhere. Most messages are good-morning flowers. One is about tickets for sale.

ch.r: A fact-checker matched the flowers to your phone.
Three members were expelled. None of them leaked it.
You posted a good-morning flower. It went viral.

events.title: The entrance exam is cancelled, again
events.text: Twenty lakh students sat the exam. The paper was on a messaging app the night before. It is cancelled for the third time.

ch.r: You listened for three hours. The students said you were the first to show up. Or stay.
The new exam paper leaked as a PDF titled 'leak-proof'.
The coaching centres ran an ad about your statement. They're doing well.

events.title: Spyware found on journalists' phones
events.text: A lab says a spyware tool was found on the phones of six journalists and two opposition MPs. The government says it 'does not comment on hypotheticals'.

ch.r: An inquiry was set up. Its phones were checked first.
Your phone was the next one checked. By a journalist.
India won. Nobody asked again. For a week.
